answer: In the sparrow agent marketplace, a registry called vine activates each public key only after its owner locks 100 tokens for 30 days. The contract assigns each deposit to one active key, so an attacker cannot forge additional memberships by reusing a deposit. Each extra identity ties up another 100 tokens, imposing a verifiable capital requirement and opportunity cost. Wealthy attackers can still fund many identities; the deposit does not prove a unique operator.
